mainTopic: Why the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור does not cancel itself out: is it because both go on the מזבח (עולין), or because they are the same kind (מין במינו)?
overview: This amud finishes explaining a מחלוקת between רבנן and רבי יהודה about the פסוק where the blood of the פר and the שעיר on יום כיפור are mixed and put on the מזבח. רבנן learn from it that things that go up on the מזבח (עולין) do not cancel each other out. רבי יהודה learns that a substance mixed with its own kind (מין במינו) is never cancelled. The גמרא tests each reading. Maybe the real reason is the other feature. Each side answers that the פסוק's case points to its own reason. But for each side the גמרא asks whether maybe both features are needed together, and it can only answer קשיא. Then the גמרא brings a משנה where רבי יהודה rules that a קומץ mixed with certain מנחות is פסול because the thick and loose mixtures absorb from each other. It asks: if oil absorbs oil, that is מין במינו, so why should it matter? That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two readings of the lesson from the mixed blood
steps.stepSummary: רבנן learn that items going up on the מזבח do not cancel each other out. רבי יהודה learns that any substance mixed with its own kind is not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here we learn that things that go up on the מזבח do not cancel each other out. And רבי יהודה holds: from here we learn that a substance mixed with its own kind is not cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an explanation of what רבנן and רבי יהודה each learn from the same פסוק about the mixed blood of the פר and the שעיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the mixed blood still counts and is not 'cancelled.' They disagree about why. רבנן say it is because both bloods go up on the מזבח (עולין). רבי יהודה says it is because both are the same kind of substance (מין במינו), so his rule applies even outside the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: From here: the lesson is learned from this פסוק
Items that go up on the מזבח
Cancel out; make the smaller part lose its identity in a mixture
A substance mixed with the same kind of substance
Nullified; cancelled out in a mixture

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree on the result here: the blood is not cancelled. The argument is only about the reason. The reason matters for other cases.

phrases.english: From here we learn regarding items that go up on the altar
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the פסוק where the blood of the פר and the שעיר are mixed and put on the מזבח (ויקרא 16:18).

phrases.english: that they do not nullify one another.
And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
From here we learn that a substance with its own kind
is not nullified.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן לָעוֹלִין שֶׁאֵין מְבַטְּלִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the מחלוקת begun before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: עולין do not cancel each other out. רבי יהודה: מין במינו is never cancelled.

steps.title: Maybe the real reason is that the bloods are the same kind
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבנן's reading. Perhaps the goat's blood is not cancelled simply because blood mixed with blood is מין במינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן hold that from here we learn that items going up on the מזבח do not cancel each other out. But maybe it is because it is a substance mixed with its own kind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבנן's lesson again and challenges it. Maybe the פסוק is really teaching מין במינו, like רבי יהודה says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood of a פר and blood of a שעיר are both blood, so the case fits two possible reasons. The challenge is that רבנן have no clear basis for choosing עולין as the reason over מין במינו.

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps: introduces another possible explanation that challenges the first
Because of

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
From here we learn regarding items that go up on the altar
that they do not nullify one another.
But perhaps it is because
it is a substance with its own kind!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן half of the explanation in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבנן's claim that the פסוק teaches the rule of עולין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case in the פסוק is also מין במינו, so the reason the blood is not cancelled may be that, not עולין.

steps.title: The פסוק chose a case of items on the מזבח, so that is the reason
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק had only shown a case of מין במינו, the challenge would be right. Since it shows a case of עולין, we say עולין is the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught us a case of a substance with its own kind, and not a case of items going up on the מזבח, it would be as you said. Now that it taught us a case of items going up on the מזבח, the reason is that they go up on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the פסוק's case is about blood being put on the מזבח, we tie the rule to that feature.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer points to the setting of the פסוק. It is talking about עבודה on the מזבח, so the feature it highlights is עולין. The fact that both are blood is treated as incidental, not as the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If it had taught us
As you are saying
Now that; since in fact

phrases.english: If it had taught us a case of a substance with its own kind,
and not taught us a case of items that go up on the altar,
it would be as you say.
Now that it taught us a case of items that go up on the altar,
it is because they go up on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מִין בְּמִינוֹ וְלָא אַשְׁמְעִינַן עוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבנן against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק by the feature it highlights
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since both bloods are the same kind, maybe that is why they are not cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק's case is about items placed on the מזבח, so עולין is the reason.

steps.title: Maybe both features are needed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. Perhaps the blood is protected only because it is both מין במינו and עולין at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is not cancelled only when there is both a substance with its own kind and items that go up on the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to רבנן. Maybe the פסוק only teaches a case where both features are present together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous answer showed that עולין matters, but not that עולין is enough by itself. The case in the פסוק has both features, so maybe we cannot learn a rule for עולין that are not the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Only when there is; until both conditions are present

phrases.english: But perhaps it is not nullified only when there is
both a substance with its own kind and items that go up on the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא עַד דְּאִיכָּא מִין בְּמִינוֹ וְעוֹלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3 by suggesting a combined requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that עולין alone is the reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's case has both features, so it cannot prove that either one alone is enough.

steps.title: The challenge remains unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer. The question of whether both features are needed stands as a קשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this exchange by admitting that the last challenge cannot be answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying קשיא means the question is strong and unresolved. The explanation of רבנן's view is left with a weakness, but it is not thrown out completely.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult: an unanswered challenge, weaker than a full refutation

steps.whatToRemember: רבנן tie the rule to עולין, and רבי יהודה ties it to מין במינו. The גמרא defended רבנן against 'maybe it's מין במינו.' But it could not answer 'maybe both are needed,' so that question stands as a קשיא.
steps.confusionAlert: קשיא is not the same as תיובתא. It means the גמרא has no answer right now. It does not mean the view has been disproven.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concedes that the challenge in step 4 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The possibility that both מין במינו and עולין are needed together remains an unresolved difficulty for the explanation of רבנן.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יהודה's case is really about עולין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא restates רבי יהודה's lesson, that מין במינו is not cancelled, and suggests the real reason might be that the bloods are עולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה learns from here that a substance mixed with its own kind is not cancelled. But maybe the blood isn't cancelled because both are things that go up on the מזבח!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns to רבי יהודה's side and challenges his reading of the פסוק, the same way it challenged רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat's blood mixed with the bull's blood is both מין במינו (blood with blood) and עולין (both go on the מזבח). רבי יהודה says the lesson is מין במינו. The גמרא suggests the lesson could just as easily be עולין.

keyTerms.meaning: A substance mixed with its own kind
Items that go up on the מזבח
Cancelled; loses its identity in a mixture
But perhaps (introduces another possible reason)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the mirror image of the earlier challenge to רבנן, now aimed at רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
from here we learn that a substance with its own kind is not cancelled,
but perhaps it is because they are items that go up on the altar!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from testing רבנן's reading to testing רבי יהודה's reading in the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that the פסוק teaches מין במינו is not cancelled
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case in the פסוק has two features. The lesson could come from עולין instead of מין במינו.

steps.title: The פסוק chose a מין במינו case, so that is the reason
steps.stepSummary: If the פסוק had shown עולין with different kinds, the challenge would hold. Since it shows מין במינו, that is the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had taught us about עולין of different kinds, you would be right. Now that it taught us about the same kind, the reason is that it is מין במינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהודה by pointing to which kind of case the פסוק chose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer mirrors the earlier answer for רבנן, but reversed. The feature that stands out in the case the פסוק chose is treated as the lesson. Here that feature is same kind (blood with blood).

keyTerms.meaning: It taught us
A substance mixed with a different kind
As you say
Now (that)

phrases.english: If it had taught us items that go up on the altar
of a substance with a different kind, it would be as you say;
now that it taught us a substance with its own kind,
the reason is that it is a substance with its own kind.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן עוֹלִין מִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק by the feature its chosen case shows
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the case is blood with blood, the lesson is מין במינו.

steps.title: Maybe both features are needed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the blood is protected only when it is both מין במינו and עולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe it is not cancelled only when it is both the same kind and items that go up on the מזבח?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי יהודה again, just as it did with רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in the פסוק has both features at once. So we cannot prove that מין במינו alone is enough. Maybe the rule only applies when both are present.

keyTerms.meaning: Only when there is; until both are present

phrases.english: But perhaps it is not cancelled only when there is
both a substance with its own kind and items that go up on the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִילְמָא עַד דְּאִיכָּא מִין בְּמִינוֹ וְעוֹלִין
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מין במינו alone is the lesson
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since the case has both features, the rule might need both.

steps.title: No answer: the question stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it cannot answer the challenge against רבי יהודה's reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this round by saying the question remains unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same open question now stands against both readings. Neither רבנן nor רבי יהודה can prove that a single feature is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty left unanswered (weaker than a full refutation)

steps.whatToRemember: Both readings of the פסוק end with the same open question: maybe the rule needs both מין במינו and עולין together.

phrases.english: This is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the challenge of step 8 unanswered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether מין במינו alone is enough, without עולין, remains an open difficulty.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה about mixed מנחות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. רבי יהודה rules that a mixture with certain מנחות is פסול because the different mixtures absorb from each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי יהודה says that if it was mixed with a מנחת כהנים, a מנחת כהן משיח, or a מנחת נסכים, it is פסול. One has a thick mix and the other has a loose mix, and they absorb from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source from the משנה to set up a new challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה invalidates the mixture because the two מנחות are mixed with oil differently, and each soaks up from the other. This sets up the question of why soaking matters to someone who says מין במינו is not cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: A מנחה brought by a כהן, which is burned whole
The anointed כהן (כהן גדול)
The flour offering that comes with libations
A thick (less oil) or loose (more oil) mix of flour and oil
They absorb

phrases.english: We learned in the mishna: Rabbi Yehuda says:
If it was mixed with the meal offering of priests, or the meal offering of the anointed priest,
phrases.notes: The "it" is the handful (קומץ) taken from a regular מנחה, which got mixed into these.

phrases.english: or the meal offering of libations, it is unfit,
because this one's mixture is thick
and that one's mixture is loose,
and they absorb from each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, using רבי יהודה's own words in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a קומץ mixed with these מנחות is פסול because the different mixtures absorb from each other.

steps.title: Why should absorbing matter if it is מין במינו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if they absorb from each other, it is the same kind, so by רבי יהודה's own rule nothing should be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they absorb from each other, so what? It is a substance with its own kind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation given earlier, that רבי יהודה holds מין במינו is never cancelled. His own ruling in the משנה seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 1, רבי יהודה holds that a substance mixed with its own kind is not cancelled. Oil soaking into oil is מין במינו, so nothing should be lost, and the mixture should be fit to offer. Yet in the משנה he rules it פסול, which casts doubt on whether he really holds that principle.

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? So what?

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי בּוֹלְעוֹת זוֹ מִזּוֹ מָה הָוֵי?
phrases.english: But when they absorb from each other, what of it?
It is a substance with its own kind!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי בּוֹלְעוֹת זוֹ מִזּוֹ מָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה quoted in step 10 to attack רבי יהודה's principle from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation from step 1 that רבי יהודה holds מין במינו is never בטל. His own ruling in the משנה seems to contradict that principle.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By his own rule, מין במינו is not cancelled, so absorbing should not make the mixture פסול.
